El Trastorno del Espectro Autista (TEA): Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a different way in which some people perceive, feel, and relate to the world. It is not an illness, but a condition that is present from childhood and accompanies the person throughout their life. Each person with ASD is unique: some may need more support in their daily lives, while others are more independent. That is why it is called a "spectrum", because characteristics and needs can vary greatly from person to person.
El TEA suele manifestarse antes de los 3: ASD usually manifests before 3 years of age. As a neurodevelopmental condition, it is present throughout a person's life. Some children show signs from the first 12 months, while in others these become more evident around 24 months or later.
Cuentan con comunicación verbal fluida y: They have fluent verbal communication and full cognitive abilities. However, they present difficulties in initiating social interactions and atypical responses. They face challenges in organizing, planning, and adapting to sudden shifts in routine.
Habilidades sociales avanzadas, autonomí: Advanced social skills, autonomy, and cognitive flexibility.
Las deficiencias en la comunicación verb: Deficiencies in verbal and non-verbal communication are evident even with visual supports. They usually communicate with simple phrases and their interactions are limited to very specific interests. They show anxiety or visible discomfort when interrupted.
Sistemas aumentativos de comunicación, r: Augmentative communication systems, emotional regulation, and predictable routines.
Alteraciones graves de la comunicación y: Severe impairments in communication and behavior causing major dysfunctions in daily functioning. Includes most cases of non-verbal autism, exhibiting high resistance to change and constant repetitive behaviors.
Comunicación funcional básica (PECS), as: Basic functional communication (PECS), assistance in essential activities, and sensory integration.
El TEA en las diferentes etapas de la vi: ASD across different stages of life
En esta etapa suelen hacerse evidentes l: During this stage, the first characteristics of ASD usually become evident. Early detection and intervention favor the development of communicative, social, and adaptive skills. Depending on individual needs, interventions such as speech therapy, occupational therapy, or applied behavior analysis (ABA) may be recommended.
Durante la adolescencia pueden presentar: During adolescence, challenges related to social interaction, communication, and adaptation to the changes typical of this stage may arise. Supports aimed at strengthening autonomy, social skills, and adaptation to new environments may also be required.
En la adultez, las necesidades de apoyo: In adulthood, support needs depend on the characteristics and circumstances of each person. Some individuals manage to function with greater autonomy in areas such as study, work, and independent living, while others continue to require support in different areas of their lives.
El tratamiento para el TEA no es único,: Treatment for ASD is not a one-size-fits-all approach; instead, it combines different personalized, interdisciplinary approaches to improve each person's development, communication, autonomy, and social participation.
Se enfocan en enseñar nuevas habilidades: They focus on teaching new skills and behaviors through positive reinforcement. Common examples include Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), which helps improve communication and reduce challenging behaviors.
Se centran en mejorar habilidades especí: They focus on improving specific developmental skills, such as speech, language, and physical abilities. They include speech therapy and occupational therapy, oriented toward daily autonomy.
Intervenciones que se integran en el ent: Interventions integrated into the school environment. They use structured visual systems (such as the TEACCH method) to help students better understand their routines and academic activities.
Buscan mejorar las habilidades sociales: They seek to improve social skills and build emotional bonds. They focus on interactive play, circles of friends, and the development of group empathy dynamics.
Aunque no curan el TEA, ciertos medicame: Although they do not cure ASD, certain medications prescribed by specialists can help manage co-occurring symptoms such as high anxiety, hyperactivity, or severe sleep problems.
La terapia cognitivo-conductual (TCC) ay: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) helps individuals understand the relationship between their thoughts, feelings, and behaviors, facilitating the management of daily emotions.
Planes alimenticios supervisados por pro: Dietary plans supervised by professionals to ensure proper nutrient absorption, especially when there are highly selective eating patterns or gastrointestinal issues.
Actividades terapéuticas integrales que: Comprehensive therapeutic activities that enrich the individual's well-being, such as equine-assisted therapy, animal-assisted therapy, art therapy, or music therapy.

Pon a prueba tus conocimientos, evalúa s: Test your knowledge, assess clinical warning signs, or train your social inclusion skills in real time through our three gamified modules.

Un compañero con TEA comienza a taparse: A classmate with ASD starts covering their ears tightly and flapping their hands due to the school bell noise. What would you do?
Gritarle para que se calme y preste aten: Yell at them to calm down and pay attention.
Guiarlo con calma hacia un espacio con m: Calmly guide them to a space with less noise and fewer stimuli.
Ignorarlo por completo para que se acost: Ignore them completely so they get used to the environment.
Reducir la sobrecarga sensorial alejándo: Reducing sensory overload by taking them away from the noise is the key step to prevent an excessive stimulation crisis.
Durante una actividad en equipo, notas q: During a team activity, you notice that a student with ASD prefers to work alone and avoids looking at others. Which approach is the most empathetic?
Exigirle que participe mirando a los ojo: Demand that they participate while making eye contact like their peers.
Respetar su espacio y ofrecerle un rol a: Respect their space and offer an alternative role where they feel comfortable.
Excluirlo del equipo para no retrasar el: Exclude them from the team so as not to delay the work.
La empatía compasiva implica respetar la: Compassionate empathy implies respecting communication differences and offering safe integration alternatives.
En el recreo, un niño con TEA repite una: At recess, a child with ASD repeats a phrase over and over (echolalia) while moving an object in their hands. How would you act?
Decirle de forma cortante que deje de re: Tell them bluntly to stop repeating that.
Comprender que es su forma de autorregul: Understand that it is their way of self-regulation and allow them their space without judgment.
Quitarle el objeto para que interactúe c: Take the object away so they interact with the other games.
Los movimientos repetitivos y la ecolali: Repetitive movements and echolalia are usually vital mechanisms of self-regulation in the face of anxiety or emotion.
Tienes que explicar un cambio repentino: You have to explain a sudden change in the day's school routine. What is the best way to communicate it to them?
Decírselo de imprevisto en el momento pa: Tell them unexpectedly at the moment so they learn to be flexible.
Anticipárselo visualmente o con antelaci: Anticipate it visually or in advance by explaining the changes step by step.
No decirle nada para evitar que se preoc: Say nothing to avoid worrying them ahead of time.
La anticipación visual y estructurada re: Visual and structured anticipation drastically reduces anxiety generated by uncertainty in people with ASD.
Un padre te comenta que su hijo se sient: A parent tells you that their child feels overwhelmed at noisy birthday parties. What ally advice would you give them?
Obligarlo a quedarse toda la fiesta para: Force them to stay the whole party to overcome their social fear.
Permitirle retirarse a una zona tranquil: Allow them to withdraw to a quiet area or plan short breaks during the event.
Prohibirle asistir a cualquier evento so: Prohibit them from attending any social events from then on.
Establecer zonas de escape o tiempos reg: Establishing escape zones or regulated times allows healthy socialization without leading to sensory exhaustion.

El autismo es una enfermedad mental que: Autism is a mental illness that can be cured with medical treatment.
Falso. El autismo no es una enfermedad n: False. Autism is neither an illness nor can it be 'cured'; it is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition.
Las personas autistas pueden desarrollar: Autistic people can develop an independent and successful work life.
Verdadero. Con los apoyos adecuados, acc: True. With the right support, accessibility, and empathetic environments, many autistic people achieve great autonomy.
Todas las personas autistas tienen habil: All autistic people have extraordinary skills in mathematics or calculation.
Falso. Esto es un estereotipo mediático: False. This is a media stereotype (the 'savant' myth). The spectrum is extremely diverse.
La sobrecarga sensorial puede causar cri: Sensory overload can cause meltdowns in some autistic people.
Verdadero. Estímulos intensos (luces, ru: True. Intense stimuli (lights, noises, crowds) can saturate the sensory system and trigger a crisis.
Las personas autistas no sienten empatía: Autistic people do not feel empathy or care to relate to others.
Falso. Sí sienten empatía, a menudo prof: False. They do feel empathy, often deeply; what may vary is how they express or interpret it.
El autismo se diagnostica principalmente: Autism is diagnosed primarily through clinical observation and behavioral development.
Verdadero. No existe un análisis de sang: True. There is no blood test or medical imaging to detect it; diagnosis is based on behavioral guidelines and interviews.
Cualquier persona puede volverse autista: Anyone can become autistic due to traumatic experiences in adulthood.
Falso. El autismo es congénito y acompañ: False. Autism is congenital and accompanies a person from birth or early childhood.
Los sistemas de comunicación aumentativa: Augmentative and alternative communication systems help non-speaking autistic people express themselves.
Verdadero. Herramientas visuales, pictog: True. Visual tools, pictograms, or technological devices greatly facilitate communication.
Las rutinas repetitivas o la necesidad d: Repetitive routines or the need for predictability are common characteristics in autism.
Verdadero. Las rutinas aportan orden, se: True. Routines provide order, security, and reduce anxiety in the face of an environment that can be unpredictable.
El autismo afecta exactamente igual a ho: Autism affects men and women in exactly the same way in its behavioral manifestation.
Falso. Las mujeres y niñas autistas suel: False. Autistic women and girls tend to camouflage or mask their traits better, which often delays their diagnosis.
